question: What is goodwill? Explain the factors that affect the value of goodwill of a partnership firm and name the common methods of valuing it.
sources: Standard accounting principles for partnership accounts: nature and valuation of goodwill (ICAI Foundation syllabus)

points.label: Meaning of goodwill
points.description: Goodwill is the value of a firm's reputation and connections that lets it earn more than a normal return on its capital; it is an intangible asset that is not fictitious.

points.label: Business-related factors
points.description: Nature of the business, favourable location, efficiency of management, and access to supplies or special advantages such as patents and licences.
points.basis: Accounting principle: factors affecting the value of goodwill

points.label: Market-related factors
points.description: Market position and competition, steady customer base, and the trend and stability of past profits.
points.basis: Accounting principle: factors affecting the value of goodwill

points.label: Valuation methods
points.description: Average profit method (simple or weighted), super profit method (super profit multiplied by a number of years), annuity method, and capitalisation method (of average profit or of super profit).
points.basis: Accounting principle: methods of valuation of goodwill
